statement: Let P be any finite set of nonzero admissible dual-lattice momentum classes modulo sign such that all source and target classes {[p],[2p]:[p] in P} are pairwise disjoint and retained. Reveal every source before its target and use the actual 12-real-coordinate affine predictable controls h_[2p]=H_p xi_[p]. At the zero-control centered stationary common-even covariance-matched A1/A6/A7 law with a fixed finite cutoff, positive floor, and common-even scalar regulator multipliers bounded by one, the complete covariance-normal endpoint has mixed Hessian blocks only on factor-three resonances [q]=[3p] or [p]=[3q]. The resonance graph is a union of finite paths. The exact R-130/R-151 envelopes give diagonal loss L(x)=624(7083/2000)x/[4096 f(x)f(4x)] and edge norm E(x)=2256(7083/2000)x/[4096 sqrt(f(x)f(4x)f(9x)f(36x))]. Exact rational Sturm certificates and an independent dyadic Bernstein audit prove one global block-row lower bound: after the 9/10 Cameron-Martin source Hessian is paid once and the whole global positive-semidefinite sixth-power Hessian is dropped, the augmented origin Hessian is strictly greater than (1/40) sum_p ||H_p||_F^2. This is a restricted multi-edge theorem, not a pairwise-to-global inference. It does not cover nonzero past, overlapping or revisited roots, nonlinear feedback, finite-amplitude convexity, arbitrary progressive controls, a historical complete-low owner, cutoff/floor removal, T-050 or A13 closure, Nelson, an interacting measure, any phase or PDE verdict, or Sector-A closure.
